info.title: RTVI
info.description:
RTVI (Real-Time Voice Interface) is the protocol a client app and a Pipecat bot use to talk to each other during a session. This document describes it from the server's point of view: receiveClientMessages lists the messages a client sends, and sendServerMessages the messages the server sends.

Every message is a JSON object with the label "rtvi-ai", a type, its data, and an id on every message a client sends and on the server's answers to them. The session's transport carries messages as data messages, next to the audio and video.

A message can also have x-rtvi-enabled-by, the server setting that turns it on (a field of Pipecat's RTVIObserverParams); x-rtvi-min-client-version, the lowest client protocol version the server sends it to; and x-rtvi-deprecated, what replaces a deprecated message. x-rtvi-behaviors lists the rules the server follows across messages.

receiveClientMessages.summary: Messages the client sends to the server.

sendServerMessages.summary: Messages the server sends to the client.

client_ready.name: client-ready
client_ready.title: client-ready
client_ready.summary: Tells the server the client is ready, with the protocol version it speaks. The server answers with bot-ready.
client_ready.description: Typically sent once the transport has connected.

disconnect_bot.name: disconnect-bot
disconnect_bot.title: disconnect-bot
disconnect_bot.summary: Asks the server to end the session.
disconnect_bot.description: Disconnecting from the transport ends the session too. This message is for a client that wants to stay connected to the transport but end its conversation with the bot.

client_message.name: client-message
client_message.title: client-message
client_message.summary: A custom message for the application. The server answers with server-response or error-response.

send_text.name: send-text
send_text.title: send-text
send_text.summary: Text the user typed, sent to the bot as if the user had said it.

send_file.name: send-file
send_file.title: send-file
send_file.summary: A file for the bot, with text that goes with it.

llm_function_call_result.name: llm-function-call-result
llm_function_call_result.title: llm-function-call-result
llm_function_call_result.summary: The result of a function call the client ran for the bot's LLM.

raw_audio.name: raw-audio
raw_audio.title: raw-audio
raw_audio.summary: A chunk of the user's audio, for transports that don't carry media.

raw_audio_batch.name: raw-audio-batch
raw_audio_batch.title: raw-audio-batch
raw_audio_batch.summary: Several chunks of the user's audio, for transports that don't carry media.

ui_event.name: ui-event
ui_event.title: ui-event
ui_event.summary: An event from the client's UI, for a UI worker.

ui_snapshot.name: ui-snapshot
ui_snapshot.title: ui-snapshot
ui_snapshot.summary: An accessibility snapshot of the client's UI, for a UI worker.
ui_snapshot.description: Sent whenever the client's UI changes, so the bot works from what is on screen.

ui_cancel_job_group.name: ui-cancel-job-group
ui_cancel_job_group.title: ui-cancel-job-group
ui_cancel_job_group.summary: Asks the server to cancel a job group it reported with ui-job-group.
ui_cancel_job_group.description: The server cancels the group only if it reported the group as cancellable.

bot_ready.name: bot-ready
bot_ready.title: bot-ready
bot_ready.summary: Answers client-ready once the bot is ready to talk, with the protocol version the server speaks to this client, information about the bot, and what it can do. Its id is the client-ready's id.
bot_ready.description: `about` is the bot's own information: Pipecat's library and version, unless the application replaces it. An application shouldn't put anything sensitive in it.

error.name: error
error.title: error
error.summary: Reports an error in the bot, such as an AI service that failed. When fatal is true, the bot can't go on and the session ends.

error_response.name: error-response
error_response.title: error-response
error_response.summary: Answers a client message the server couldn't handle, with what went wrong. Its id is the id of the message it answers.

server_response.name: server-response
server_response.title: server-response
server_response.summary: The bot's answer to a client-message. Its id is the client-message's id, and t is the client-message's t.

server_message.name: server-message
server_message.title: server-message
server_message.summary: A message from the bot's application to the client, with data of the application's own.

data.description: The application's own data, any JSON value, as the bot's application sent it.

metrics.name: metrics
metrics.title: metrics
metrics.summary: Performance metrics of the bot's services, such as how long each took to respond and how much it processed. On by default; turned off by the server's `metrics_enabled` setting.

system_log.name: system-log
system_log.title: system-log
system_log.summary: A line of the server's log, for debugging. Off by default; turned on by the server's `system_logs_enabled` setting.

user_started_speaking.name: user-started-speaking
user_started_speaking.title: user-started-speaking
user_started_speaking.summary: The user's turn started: the bot considers the user to be speaking. On by default; turned off by the server's `user_speaking_enabled` setting.

user_stopped_speaking.name: user-stopped-speaking
user_stopped_speaking.title: user-stopped-speaking
user_stopped_speaking.summary: The user's turn ended: the bot considers the user done speaking. On by default; turned off by the server's `user_speaking_enabled` setting.

vad_user_started_speaking.name: vad-user-started-speaking
vad_user_started_speaking.title: vad-user-started-speaking
vad_user_started_speaking.summary: Voice activity detection (VAD) heard the user start speaking. It reacts to any voice, sooner than user-started-speaking, which comes when the bot decides the user's turn started. Off by default; turned on by the server's `vad_user_speaking_enabled` setting.

vad_user_stopped_speaking.name: vad-user-stopped-speaking
vad_user_stopped_speaking.title: vad-user-stopped-speaking
vad_user_stopped_speaking.summary: Voice activity detection (VAD) heard the user stop speaking. It reacts to any pause, sooner than user-stopped-speaking, which comes when the bot decides the user's turn ended. Off by default; turned on by the server's `vad_user_speaking_enabled` setting.

user_mute_started.name: user-mute-started
user_mute_started.title: user-mute-started
user_mute_started.summary: The bot stopped listening to the user, for example while it says something that must not be interrupted. On by default; turned off by the server's `user_mute_enabled` setting.
user_mute_started.description: The client should keep sending audio. It may show the user that their input isn't being processed.

user_mute_stopped.name: user-mute-stopped
user_mute_stopped.title: user-mute-stopped
user_mute_stopped.summary: The bot listens to the user again. On by default; turned off by the server's `user_mute_enabled` setting.
user_mute_stopped.description: The client may show the user that their input is being processed again.

bot_started_speaking.name: bot-started-speaking
bot_started_speaking.title: bot-started-speaking
bot_started_speaking.summary: The bot started speaking: its audio started playing to the user. On by default; turned off by the server's `bot_speaking_enabled` setting.

bot_stopped_speaking.name: bot-stopped-speaking
bot_stopped_speaking.title: bot-stopped-speaking
bot_stopped_speaking.summary: The bot stopped speaking. On by default; turned off by the server's `bot_speaking_enabled` setting.

bot_interrupted.name: bot-interrupted
bot_interrupted.title: bot-interrupted
bot_interrupted.summary: The bot was interrupted and stopped what it was saying. A client should drop the bot's text that hadn't been spoken yet. On by default; turned off by the server's `bot_speaking_enabled` setting.
bot_interrupted.description: The user speaking over the bot interrupts it, and so does a send-text with `run_immediately`.

user_audio_level.name: user-audio-level
user_audio_level.title: user-audio-level
user_audio_level.summary: How loud the user's audio is, from 0 (quiet) to 1 (loud), sent regularly while the user's audio comes in. Off by default; turned on by the server's `user_audio_level_enabled` setting.
user_audio_level.description: Sent every 0.15 seconds by default, the server's `audio_level_period_secs` setting.

bot_audio_level.name: bot-audio-level
bot_audio_level.title: bot-audio-level
bot_audio_level.summary: How loud the bot's audio is, from 0 (quiet) to 1 (loud), sent regularly while the bot speaks. Off by default; turned on by the server's `bot_audio_level_enabled` setting.
bot_audio_level.description: Sent every 0.15 seconds by default, the server's `audio_level_period_secs` setting.

user_input.name: user-input
user_input.title: user-input
user_input.summary: What the user said or typed: a transcription of their speech, text the client sent, or a short acknowledgment the user said while the bot talks. On by default; turned off by the server's `user_input_enabled` setting.
user_input.description: Sent for each transcription of the user's speech; for each short acknowledgment the user says while the bot talks, which neither interrupts the bot nor reaches its LLM; and for each send-text message, with the send-text's id in `msg_id`.

user_llm_text.name: user-llm-text
user_llm_text.title: user-llm-text
user_llm_text.summary: The user's message as the bot's LLM receives it. On by default; turned off by the server's `user_llm_enabled` setting.

stt_raw_text.name: stt-raw-text
stt_raw_text.title: stt-raw-text
stt_raw_text.summary: A transcription of the user's speech as the speech-to-text service produces it, including interim transcriptions that may still change. Off by default; turned on by the server's `stt_raw_text_enabled` setting. Sent only to clients of protocol 2.2.0 or later.

user_transcription.name: user-transcription
user_transcription.title: user-transcription
user_transcription.summary: A transcription of the user's speech, including interim transcriptions that may still change. On by default; turned off by the server's `user_transcription_enabled` setting. Deprecated. Use user-input or stt-raw-text instead.

bot_output.name: bot-output
bot_output.title: bot-output
bot_output.summary: Text the bot says or shows, a sentence or another unit at a time, with whether it will be spoken and how much of it has been spoken. On by default; turned off by the server's `bot_output_enabled` setting.

bot_llm_started.name: bot-llm-started
bot_llm_started.title: bot-llm-started
bot_llm_started.summary: The bot's LLM started generating a response. On by default; turned off by the server's `bot_llm_enabled` setting.

bot_llm_stopped.name: bot-llm-stopped
bot_llm_stopped.title: bot-llm-stopped
bot_llm_stopped.summary: The bot's LLM finished generating a response. On by default; turned off by the server's `bot_llm_enabled` setting.

bot_tts_started.name: bot-tts-started
bot_tts_started.title: bot-tts-started
bot_tts_started.summary: The bot's text-to-speech service started turning a response into speech. On by default; turned off by the server's `bot_tts_enabled` setting.

bot_tts_stopped.name: bot-tts-stopped
bot_tts_stopped.title: bot-tts-stopped
bot_tts_stopped.summary: The bot's text-to-speech service finished turning a response into speech. On by default; turned off by the server's `bot_tts_enabled` setting.

llm_raw_text.name: llm-raw-text
llm_raw_text.title: llm-raw-text
llm_raw_text.summary: Text exactly as the bot's LLM streams it, a chunk at a time. Off by default; turned on by the server's `llm_raw_text_enabled` setting. Sent only to clients of protocol 2.2.0 or later.

tts_raw_text.name: tts-raw-text
tts_raw_text.title: tts-raw-text
tts_raw_text.summary: Text the bot's text-to-speech service speaks, as it speaks it. Off by default; turned on by the server's `tts_raw_text_enabled` setting. Sent only to clients of protocol 2.2.0 or later.

bot_llm_marker.name: bot-llm-marker
bot_llm_marker.title: bot-llm-marker
bot_llm_marker.summary: The marker the bot's LLM put in a response, outside the text it speaks, such as one saying whether the user's turn was complete. Sent once per response, when it ends. Off by default; turned on by the server's `bot_llm_marker_enabled` setting.
bot_llm_marker.description: It carries the raw text of the whole response, so it's meant for evaluation and debugging rather than for the user.

bot_transcription.name: bot-transcription
bot_transcription.title: bot-transcription
bot_transcription.summary: The text of the bot's LLM response, a whole sentence at a time. On by default; turned off by the server's `bot_llm_enabled` setting.
bot_transcription.description: It carries no timing. For text as the bot speaks it, use tts-raw-text.

bot_llm_text.name: bot-llm-text
bot_llm_text.title: bot-llm-text
bot_llm_text.summary: Text as the bot's LLM streams it, a chunk at a time. On by default; turned off by the server's `bot_llm_enabled` setting. Deprecated. Use llm-raw-text instead.

bot_tts_text.name: bot-tts-text
bot_tts_text.title: bot-tts-text
bot_tts_text.summary: Text the bot's text-to-speech service speaks, as it speaks it. On by default; turned off by the server's `bot_tts_enabled` setting. Deprecated. Use tts-raw-text instead.

bot_llm_search_response.name: bot-llm-search-response
bot_llm_search_response.title: bot-llm-search-response
bot_llm_search_response.summary: The bot's LLM grounded its answer in a web search: the answer, and the sites each part of it came from.

data.search_result: Lisbon is sunny today, with a high of 24°C.

results.text: Lisbon is sunny today, with a high of 24°C.

bot_llm_search_response.description: Only an LLM service that reports its searches sends it: in Pipecat, the Google LLM services, with `GoogleRTVIProcessor` in place of `RTVIProcessor`.

llm_function_call_started.name: llm-function-call-started
llm_function_call_started.title: llm-function-call-started
llm_function_call_started.summary: The bot's LLM started calling a function. The server's settings decide whether it includes the function's name.
llm_function_call_started.description: The server's report level for the function decides whether it carries the function's name: `name`, `arguments` and `full` do, and `none` doesn't. At `disabled`, the server sends no messages about the call.

llm_function_call_in_progress.name: llm-function-call-in-progress
llm_function_call_in_progress.title: llm-function-call-in-progress
llm_function_call_in_progress.summary: A function call is running, with its id and, as the server's settings decide, the function's name and arguments.
llm_function_call_in_progress.description: How much it carries depends on the server's report level for the function: `none` sends only the call's id, `name` adds the function's name, `arguments` its arguments, and `full` its result. At `disabled`, the server sends no messages about the call. A client that runs the function itself answers with llm-function-call-result.

llm_function_call_stopped.name: llm-function-call-stopped
llm_function_call_stopped.title: llm-function-call-stopped
llm_function_call_stopped.summary: A function call finished or was cancelled, with its id and, as the server's settings decide, the function's name and result.
llm_function_call_stopped.description: How much it carries depends on the server's report level for the function: `none` sends only the call's id, `name` adds the function's name, `arguments` its arguments, and `full` its result. At `disabled`, the server sends no messages about the call.

llm_function_call.name: llm-function-call
llm_function_call.title: llm-function-call
llm_function_call.summary: The bot's LLM called a function, with its name, id and arguments. Deprecated. Use llm-function-call-in-progress instead.

ui_command.name: ui-command
ui_command.title: ui-command
ui_command.summary: A command from the bot to the client's UI, such as showing a notification.
ui_command.description: The standard commands each have a payload of their own, and `@pipecat-ai/client-react` has a default handler for each. An application can also send commands of its own.

ui_job_group.title: ui-job-group
ui_job_group.summary: Progress of work the bot handed to other workers, for the client's UI: the work started, a worker's update or result, or all of it completed.

segment_id.description: Identifies the segment the text belongs to; every message about one segment, such as its spoken progress, carries the same id.

spoken_progress.description: **(v2+)** Accumulated / remaining text breakdown. Present when `will_be_spoken` is `true`.

delivery.description: **(2.3.0+)** The delivery of the text just spoken, by its universal names, such as `["warm", "emphasis"]`, empty for the voice's baseline. They change within a segment where its delivery does, so a segment's `"new"` message has none. Present in expressive conversation (alpha).

x-rtvi-behaviors.description: Once the bot is ready, the server answers client-ready with a bot-ready carrying the client-ready's id.
bot-ready's version is the protocol version the server speaks to the client: the server's own for a client of the same major version, and the client's own for a 1.x client.

A client-ready without a version, with a malformed one, or of a major version the server doesn't speak gets an error-response carrying its id. The session goes on, and the server still answers with bot-ready.
A client message the server can't handle, of an unknown type or with data that doesn't match its payload, gets an error-response carrying the message's id.
A transport message labeled "rtvi-ai" that isn't an RTVI message, such as one without an id, gets an error, since there is no id to answer. The server ignores a message without the "rtvi-ai" label.
The bot answers a client-message with a server-response or an error-response carrying the client-message's id. A server-response's t is the client-message's t.
The server sends a message that has x-rtvi-enabled-by only while the server setting it names is on. The settings are fields of Pipecat's RTVIObserverParams.
bot-output for text the bot will speak waits for the bot to start speaking: the server sends it after bot-started-speaking, in the order the text came.
On an interruption, the server sends bot-interrupted, and never sends the bot-output it was holding for speech that the interruption cut off.
